text:
Maya: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel flip I see a latency bump for short prompts in prod. p50 went from ~42ms -> ~58ms for the 8-32 token cohort. Throughput steady, but batch formation looks different. Anyone else seeing KV hit-rate drop too?
perf-bot: Autoprof run finished for roll 2026-03-18. Summary: KV cache hit-rate down 11% on prompt-length 8-32, decode-rate bucket 'fast' saw +18% tail latency. Kernel selection: fallback to generic GEMM for microbatches when batch_size < 6.
Zack: I think the batcher is merging tiny requests across decode-rate strata and forcing non-optimized kernels. Current token-budget target is 128ms window which lets very short prompts hang around too long.
Anika: Possible quick wins: 1) tighten prompt-length buckets so very-short don't co-mingle with mid-short. 2) lower token-budget for cohort 0-32 to prioritize immediate dispatch.
Liam: Agreed. Proposed new buckets: [0-16], [17-64], [65-256], [>256]. Also suggest decode-rate buckets: fast(>250 tok/s), mid(80-250), slow(<80). That way we avoid combining a 12-token 400 tok/s request with a 100-token 50 tok/s one.
Maya: Can you sketch the batcher config change? small example for token_budget and max_hold_ms?
Zack: Sure — rough: ```yaml
batcher:
  cohorts:
    - name: tiny
      prompt_len: [0,16]
      token_budget_ms: 20
      max_hold_ms: 5
    - name: short
      prompt_len: [17,64]
      token_budget_ms: 60
      max_hold_ms: 10
    - name: mid
      prompt_len: [65,256]
      token_budget_ms: 120
      max_hold_ms: 20
```
Anika: Also add a rule: if KV hit-rate < 80% for cohort then reduce max_hold_ms by 50% and force local-prefetch = true. That reduces useless queuing while KV warms.
Maya: Nice. Perf question: what's the impact on throughput if we drop token_budget for tiny cohort to 20ms? Have any microbench numbers?
perf-bot: Quick sim: lowering tiny token_budget_ms from 60->20 yields median latency drop ~14ms for tiny cohort, throughput at node-level -2.1% under uniform mix, +0.7% under real traffic trace (more short prompts). KV hit-rate simulated +4%.
Liam: Sounds safe as canary. Plan: canary on 10% of traffic in us-west2 for 2h with rollout criteria: p50 tiny <=45ms and node throughput drop <5%.
Maya: @deploy-bot can you schedule? Also add tracing tags for kernel_variant and batch_size in spans.
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled for 2026-03-18T14:10Z on us-west2 @ 10%. Health checks: latency, kv_hit, kernel_mismatch_rate.
Zack: One more: consider kernel-hinting for microbatches. If predicted batch size <6 and prompt_len <32, force small-kernel path to avoid runtime fallback cost. Might need a quick binary toggle in runtime.
Anika: Kernel-hinting is good but risky — let's gate behind perf-flag. If canary looks ok we enable for all cohorts where kv_hit>75% and avg_decode_rate>200 tok/s.
Maya: Action list: 1) Zack: push batcher config PR with new buckets + token_budget change (ETA 2h). 2) Anika: implement adaptive kv-hit throttle rule (ETA EOD). 3) Liam: create canary + alert playbook (ETA 1h). 4) Me: add tracing tags + perf dashboards update.
Liam: I'll also add a short smoke test to verify kernel_variant tag appears and batch_size distribution in spans looks sane.
Zack: I'll include a tiny perf bench comparing small-kernel vs fallback at batch sizes 1..8 and post numbers in thread.
Maya: Thanks all :thumbsup: Let's reconvene after canary verdict. If anyone notices regressions before roll, ping #eng-runtime and @oncall.
